 Order

This Writ Petition has been filed to direct the respondents not to interfere with the petitioner firm's functioning of restaurant along with herbal hookah services (0% tobacco & 0% nicotine) with all required statutory licenses, under the guise of incessant inspection during the working hours thereby infringing their right to do a legal business guaranteed under Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution by considering the petitioner representation dated 18.08.2025.
2.
The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner is running a restaurant under the name and style of M/s.Deja Brew Care after obtaining required licenses.
It is further stated that a separate earmarked smoking area has been provided for serving herbal flavour hookah without any content or traces of Tobacco or Nicotine.

The petitioner has also obtained license from FSSAI on 04.12.2024 which is valid up to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 16/09/2025 04:41:11 pm )
03.12.2025.

According to the petitioner, the respondents have been frequently interfering with the petitioner's business under the guise of inspection during business hours and disrupted the functioning in front of the customers.
Hence, the present petition has been filed.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the third respondent police for conducting periodical inspection of the petitioner firm.
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents filed a Counter Affidavit.
5. In the counter statement, it is specifically denied that the respondent police had caused any disturbance to the petitioner's business.

It has been stated that earlier, the petitioner had filed a Writ Petition in W.P.No.39716 of 2024 seeking to forbear the third respondent police herein from interfering in relation to the running of their restaurant in which, this Court by order dated 27.12.2024 had passed the following order:
"4.

In view of the said submissions made by either parties, there shall be a direction to the petitioner forthwith to make an application before the Department of Food M/S.Deja Brew Cafe vs The Commissioner Of Police on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168268222/
2 Safety and obtain an appropriate permission for providing Herbal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 16/09/2025 04:41:11 pm ) Hookah Services (without any content or trace of tobacco and nicotine).

sentences.text: The petitioner shall also give an under taking letter before the respondent police to have separate smoking area for servicing Herbal Hookah Services (without any content or trace of Tobacco and Nicotine).
On receipt of the said undertaking, the respondent police are directed not to interfere with the business premises of the petitioner after getting permission by the Department of Food Safety.
5. It is made clear that the petitioner will strictly adhere the undertaking and will not violate it by taking advantage of the order passed by this Court.
I also further make it clear that it will not prevent the respondent police for making the periodical inspection as to whether the undertaking is followed by the petitioner.
On 31.05.2025 at about 1.00 p.m., the third respondent police received an information that the owner of Herbal Hookah Service, illegally supplying tobacco products in the restaurant.
On receipt of the intimation, the Sub Inspector of Police along with his team went to the restaurant and conducted search in the restaurant and seized 1. Soex Blueberry flavour- 500 gram (1 box); 2.
Soex Pan Raas Flavour-400 grams (1 box);

3.Soex https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
16/09/2025 04:41:11 pm ) Maghai Paan Flavour-450 gram (1 box); 4. Soex Orange Flavour-400 gram (1 box) and 5. Soex Mint Flavour-450 gram (1 box) and also registered a case in Crime No.345 of 2025 for the offence under Section 21 (A) of Cigarette and other Tobacco Products Act 2003.

sentences.text:
During the course of investigation,
the respondent police produced the seized contraband before the Concerned Court and that the petitioner has been continuously indulging in such illegal activities.
Therefore, for the interest and safety of the public, the police had instructed the petitioner to close the bar.
Despite several oral instructions, the management did not comply with the instructions.
The respondent police were not disturbing the business of the petitioner.

Since already there is an FIR registered against the petitioner, on receipt of secret credible informations that the petitioner again served hookah with harmful, prohibited content of tobacco/nicotine, the police personnel inspected the restaurant.
Liberty is given to the respondents to undertake a surprise inspection.

6. In view of the above, though the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is not using any tobacco or nicotine products in the earmarked smoking area for serving herbal flavor hookah, the fact remains that already a case has been registered against the petitioner.

Whether the so-called herbal products, as claimed by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 16/09/2025 04:41:11 pm ) petitioner, contain nicotine or not, can only be determined by experts and not by this Court.
This Court cannot proceed merely on the basis of oral submissions.
7. It is the consistent stand of the respondents that they are not disturbing the petitioner in running the restaurant.

If the petitioner is of the view that his products do not contain any tobacco or nicotine, it is for the petitioner to satisfy the competent Authorities particularly Food Safety and M/S.Deja Brew Cafe vs The Commissioner Of Police on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168268222/
3 Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).
8.

sentences.text: In this regard, by way of amendment brought by the State Government under L.A.Bill No.57 of 2022, Section 4A was introduced, which prohibits hookah bars.
Therefore, whether the petitioner's hookah contains tobacco or not is an issue that has to be determined by the competent authority.

9. On considering the provisions of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act,
2003 and Food Safety and Standards Act, if the product used in the hookah is tobacco containing nicotine, it will fall under the COTPA Act.

Therefore, if at all the petitioner herein wants to run an enclosed zone for herbal hookah, first of all, he has to satisfy that his trade is not in a public place which includes restaurant and does not fall under the prohibition of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act.

entities.text: Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10. He cannot use tobacco or any product containing nicotine, in view of the prohibition under Section 4(A) of the COTPA Act, and in case if we want to use any other product other than product containing nicotine and claims it to be a herbal product, it must be in satisfaction with the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
11. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to approach FSSAI Authorities and place before them all the ingredients used in the preparation of hookah in his premises.
The Food Safety Officer may draw samples and send them to a laboratory for testing.
If it is satisfied that the products do not contain any tobacco or nicotine, the petitioner is at liberty to continue his business in respect of running of the hookah bar.
12. Insofar as the running of the restaurant is concerned, the respondents shall not interfere with the petitioner's business.
However, it is made clear that the respondents Police are at liberty to take action if any illegal activities are found to be carried on in the petitioner's premises.

13. Accordingly, this Writ Petition (Criminal) stands disposed of with the aforesaid directions.
